Near you, wherever you are

## An SEO Expert Near You, Wherever You Are

If you'd like someone close by, I'm in Himachal Pradesh, not far from Shimla, and happy to meet local businesses in person. If you're further away, we'll work over video calls. Either way, you're talking to the person actually doing the work.

About

## Hello, I'm Anil.

I've worked in SEO and paid ads since 2011. I started in agency teams, went independent in 2018, and today I run two agencies of my own: Zorvex Technologies and Uniq Web Infotech. I still work hands-on in every ad account, analytics setup and website I look after.

Home is a village in the hills of Himachal Pradesh. My clients are mostly in the US, UK and Australia, and we talk over Zoom, Google Meet and WhatsApp, in English, Hindi or Punjabi.

## Experience

Fourteen years of SEO, from analyst to founder.

The process

## How We’ll Work

Four steps, no surprises. You'll always know what I'm doing, why, and whether it's working.

- 01

### Audit

I review your website, rankings, ads, Google Business Profile and analytics end to end, and find what’s holding you back.

You getA written audit and a prioritised fix list

- 02

### Strategy

We agree the plan together: priorities, budgets and the KPIs that matter. Nothing changes without your approval.

You getA clear roadmap with targets

- 03

### Launch

I put it to work myself: SEO fixes, content, ad campaigns or a new website, delivered on schedule.

You getA change log you can read any time

- 04

### Optimise & report

Ongoing testing to keep improving results, with a monthly report in plain English: what moved, why, and what’s next.

You getA monthly report, every month

Not sure where to start? Start with an audit.

SEO Services

# SEO Expert in Himachal, Working With Businesses Near and Far

Rankings are nice, but what you really want is the phone ringing and orders coming in. That's what I work towards. I've been doing SEO since 2011, from a small village in Himachal near Shimla, and I still do every audit, fix and report myself.

★★★★★ Top Rated Plus · 100% Job Success · 1,000+ five-star reviews

What’s included

## What you get

No account managers, no hand-offs. I do the work myself, start to finish.

### SEO audit

A full crawl of your site: indexing, speed, Core Web Vitals, internal links, duplicate content and schema, written up as a prioritised fix list.

### Keyword research

The terms your buyers actually search, grouped by intent, so every page has a clear job.

### Technical SEO

Fixes for crawl errors, redirects, canonicals, sitemaps, page speed and structured data.

### On-page optimisation

Titles, meta descriptions, headings, copy and internal links tuned for each target keyword.

### Content planning

A content calendar built around topics that rank and convert, planned and written by me.

### Link building

Relevant, earned links from real websites through outreach, never link farms.

The process

## How I Work

First, I look properly at your site, your rankings and your analytics. Then I tell you, in plain words, what's holding you back and what I'd fix first. Nothing changes until you've agreed the plan.

After that it's steady, visible work. You can open the change log any time and see exactly what I did and when. Once a month you get a short report: what moved, why it moved, and what's next.

- 01LookI go through what you have and find what's holding you back.

- 02PlanWe agree what to do first and what it should achieve.

- 03DoI make the changes and launch the campaigns myself.

- 04Improve & reportI keep testing, and send you a short monthly update.

## SEO vs. Paid Advertising

Most of my clients use both. Ads bring in customers this month; SEO makes every customer cheaper next year.

### SEO

Builds rankings you own. It takes a few months to compound, but the traffic keeps coming without paying for every click.

### Paid ads

Buys visibility from day one and is ideal for testing offers, but stops the moment the budget does.

Near you

## Being found by people nearby

When someone close by searches for what you sell, Google leans on three things: your Google Business Profile, your reviews, and whether your site clearly says what you do and where. I work on all three. It's the same whether your customers are in Shimla or in a town in Texas.

Google Ads Management

# Google Ads Management by a Certified Expert

With Google Ads, the only number that really matters is what each lead or sale costs you. I set up and run campaigns with that number in mind, and I always start by making sure the tracking is telling the truth.

★★★★★ Top Rated Plus · 100% Job Success · 1,000+ five-star reviews

What’s included

## What you get

No account managers, no hand-offs. I do the work myself, start to finish.

### Account audit

Where the budget is going today, what is wasted, and the quick wins.

### Search campaigns

Keyword research, tight ad groups, responsive search ads and negative keyword lists.

### Shopping & Merchant Center

Feed fixes, product groups and Shopping campaigns for e-commerce stores.

### Performance Max

Asset groups, audience signals and search themes, set up so PMax doesn't simply eat branded traffic.

### Conversion tracking

GA4, Google Tag Manager, enhanced conversions and call tracking, so bidding learns from real results.

### Reporting

A monthly report on spend, conversions, cost per lead and ROAS, plus what I'm testing next.

The process

## How I Work

The first thing I check is your conversion tracking. Google's bidding learns from it, so if it's broken or counting things twice, the account is learning the wrong lessons. I fix that before touching anything else.

Then I build or tidy up the campaigns around what you actually want: calls, form leads or online sales. Every week I go through search terms, bids, ads and landing pages, and cut what's wasting money.

- 01LookI go through what you have and find what's holding you back.

- 02PlanWe agree what to do first and what it should achieve.

- 03DoI make the changes and launch the campaigns myself.

- 04Improve & reportI keep testing, and send you a short monthly update.

## Google Ads vs. Other Paid Channels

Search catches people who already want what you sell; social ads find people who don't know they want it yet. The right mix depends on your product and budget, and I'll tell you which I'd start with.

### Google Ads

Reaches people at the moment they search. You pay per click, and intent is high.

### Social ads

Meta, Pinterest and LinkedIn build demand among people who aren't searching yet, priced per impression or per click.

Near you

## Spending only where your customers are

If people need to visit or call you, there's no point paying for clicks from the other side of the country. I set your ads to the areas you actually serve, add your phone number and address, and cut the places that waste money.

Title: Facebook Ads Expert in Himachal Pradesh | Anil Sharma
Description: Facebook and Meta Ads expert: prospecting, retargeting, catalogue ads, Pixel and Conversions API setup for e-commerce and lead generation.

Facebook & Meta Ads

# Facebook Ads That Bring In Real Customers

Facebook and Instagram ads work well when two things are right: the data Meta gets back from your site, and the ads themselves. I sort out the tracking first, then build campaigns that find new customers and remind the ones who nearly bought.

★★★★★ Top Rated Plus · 100% Job Success · 1,000+ five-star reviews

What’s included

## What you get

No account managers, no hand-offs. I do the work myself, start to finish.

### Pixel & Conversions API

Server-side tracking so Meta sees your sales and leads despite browser restrictions.

### Prospecting campaigns

Broad and interest-based audiences, Advantage+ campaigns and lookalikes to reach new buyers.

### Retargeting

Ads for people who viewed products, added to cart or started a form.

### Catalogue ads

Dynamic product ads from your Shopify or WooCommerce catalogue.

### Creative testing

A steady rhythm of new images, videos and copy, with clear winners and losers.

### Reporting

Cost per result, ROAS and what changed each month, matched against your own sales data.

The process

## How I Work

I start by checking that your Pixel and Conversions API are recording sales and leads correctly, with nothing counted twice. If Meta can't see who buys, it can't find more people like them.

I keep campaigns simple: a few well-funded ad sets rather than dozens of tiny ones. Then I keep testing new images, videos and copy, because the creative is usually what makes the difference.

- 01LookI go through what you have and find what's holding you back.

- 02PlanWe agree what to do first and what it should achieve.

- 03DoI make the changes and launch the campaigns myself.

- 04Improve & reportI keep testing, and send you a short monthly update.

## Paid vs. Organic Facebook

They work best together. Your posts build trust with people who already follow you; ads put that trust in front of people who don't know you yet.

### Organic

Free, and good for community and trust, but reach is small and unpredictable.

### Paid

Reaches exactly who you choose, at the scale you choose, with results you can measure.

Near you

## Reaching people in your area

For a local business, I target the towns or the radius around you where your customers live. Once the Pixel has enough data, I add lookalike audiences of people similar to the ones who already buy.

Based in Himachal · Happy to meet locally · Working remotely with clients in the US, UK and Australia

Instagram Ads

# Instagram Ads for Feed, Stories and Reels

People scroll Instagram fast, so an ad has about a second to earn attention. I plan ads that suit each spot, whether that's Feed, Stories or Reels, and judge them on sales and leads, not likes.

★★★★★ Top Rated Plus · 100% Job Success · 1,000+ five-star reviews

What’s included

## What you get

No account managers, no hand-offs. I do the work myself, start to finish.

### Targeting

Interest, lookalike, broad and retargeting audiences matched to your customer.

### Placements

Creative sized and written for Feed, Stories and Reels instead of one asset stretched everywhere.

### Creative direction

Hooks, copy and format guidance for images, carousels and short video.

### Shopping ads

Product tags and catalogue ads for e-commerce stores.

### Tracking

Pixel and Conversions API events so results show up correctly.

### Analytics

Monthly reporting on cost per result and return on ad spend.

The process

## How I Work

Instagram ads run through the same Meta account as Facebook, so I plan both together. That stops two campaigns bidding against each other for the same person.

I test new creative often. On Instagram, the image or video does more of the work than the targeting does.

- 01LookI go through what you have and find what's holding you back.

- 02PlanWe agree what to do first and what it should achieve.

- 03DoI make the changes and launch the campaigns myself.

- 04Improve & reportI keep testing, and send you a short monthly update.

## Instagram vs. Facebook Ads

Most accounts run both and let Meta decide where each ad does best. I'll set it up so you can see what each one is bringing in.

### Instagram

Visual, younger-skewing and strong for fashion, beauty, lifestyle and products that photograph well.

### Facebook

A broader audience and more placements, often cheaper per result for lead generation.

Near you

## Good for places people visit

Stories and Reels work especially well for cafés, salons, hotels and shops. Ads shown to people nearby mean the ones who see you can actually drop in.

Pinterest Ads

# Pinterest Ads for Brands People Plan Around

People go to Pinterest to plan: a new kitchen, a wedding, a gift list, next season's wardrobe. That makes it a good place to show your products while people are still making up their minds.

★★★★★ Top Rated Plus · 100% Job Success · 1,000+ five-star reviews

What’s included

## What you get

No account managers, no hand-offs. I do the work myself, start to finish.

### Pinterest tag

Base code and conversion events, checked against your store's orders.

### Keyword & interest targeting

Search terms and interests chosen from Pinterest Trends and your own data.

### Shopping campaigns

Catalogue-based product pins for Shopify and other stores.

### Seasonal campaigns

Plans for holidays and peak seasons, launched early, because Pinterest users plan ahead.

### Creative

Vertical pins with clear text overlays and product focus.

### Reporting

Clicks, saves, conversions and ROAS, compared with your other channels.

The process

## How I Work

Pinterest users plan early, so seasonal campaigns start weeks before they would on other platforms. Your pins need to be there when people start saving ideas, not when they're ready to check out.

I set up the tag and catalogue first, then test audiences and pin designs, and put more budget behind whatever sells.

- 01LookI go through what you have and find what's holding you back.

- 02PlanWe agree what to do first and what it should achieve.

- 03DoI make the changes and launch the campaigns myself.

- 04Improve & reportI keep testing, and send you a short monthly update.

## Pinterest vs. Other Paid Advertising

Pinterest is great for products that look good in a photo. I'd use it alongside Google and Meta, not instead of them.

### Pinterest Ads

Visual and discovery-led, reaching people early in their buying journey, often at lower cost per click.

### Search & social ads

Broader formats and audiences, better for demand that already exists.

Near you

## Reaching planners where you sell

I target the countries and regions where your buyers are, and time campaigns to when they start planning, not just when they buy.

# Retargeting Ads That Win Back Almost-Buyers

★★★★★ Top Rated Plus · 100% Job Success · 1,000+ five-star reviews

### Search remarketing

Bid adjustments in Google Search for past visitors.

### Customer-list audiences

Upsell and win-back campaigns built from your customer list.

### Frequency control

Caps and exclusions so people aren't followed around the internet.

### Measurement

View-through and click-through results kept separate, so the numbers stay honest.

The process

## How I Work

The message changes over time: first a reminder, then a reason to come back, then reviews from other customers. And I cap how often people see your ads, because nobody likes being followed around the internet.

- 04Improve & reportI keep testing, and send you a short monthly update.

### SEO

Brings new visitors to your site from search over time.

### Retargeting

Turns more of those visitors into customers after they leave.

URL: https://anilsharma.co/effective-onpage-seo-techniques/
Title: 10 On-Page SEO Techniques to Boost Your Website's Visibility
Description: Ten on-page SEO techniques that still work in 2026: keyword research, titles, headings, content, speed, URLs, internal links, images, schema and mobile.

On-page SEO just means everything you control on the page itself. Get it right and Google understands your page better, and so do the people reading it. These are the ten things I check on every site I work on.

## 1. Start with keyword research

Find the terms your audience actually searches for, and decide which page should rank for each. Google Keyword Planner, Ahrefs, Semrush and Moz all help. Map one main keyword, plus close variations, to each page.

## 2. Write strong titles and meta descriptions

Your title tag is the headline in search results, so include the target keyword and make it worth clicking.

- Keep titles to around 60 characters

- Keep meta descriptions to around 155 characters

- Write unique titles and descriptions for every page

## 3. Use headings to structure the page

Use one H1 for the main topic, H2s for sections and H3s for sub-sections. Clear structure helps readers scan and helps search engines, including AI search, understand the page.

## 4. Write content that answers the search

Content should match search intent and be genuinely useful.

- Use keywords naturally, without stuffing

- Keep paragraphs short and use lists

- Add original images, examples and data

- Answer the questions people ask next

## 5. Make the site fast

Speed affects rankings and conversions. Compress images, serve modern formats such as WebP, minify CSS and JavaScript, enable caching and use a CDN. Check Core Web Vitals in Search Console.

## 6. Keep URLs short and descriptive

Use lowercase words separated by hyphens, include the main keyword and avoid dates, numbers and symbols where possible.

## 7. Link between your own pages

Internal links show search engines which pages matter and help visitors find related content. Use descriptive anchor text and link where it genuinely helps.

## 8. Optimise images and video

Compress files, write descriptive alt text, add captions where useful and set width and height so pages don't jump while loading.

## 9. Add schema markup

Structured data helps search engines understand your page and can enable rich results such as reviews, prices and FAQs. Validate it with Google's Rich Results Test and keep it accurate.

## 10. Design for mobile first

Google indexes the mobile version of your site. Use responsive design, readable font sizes and tap targets that are easy to hit.

This isn't a one-off job. Every few months, look at Search Console for pages sitting just off page one, and give those some attention first. Small fixes there often pay off quickest. Get in touch.

URL: https://anilsharma.co/how-to-rank-for-local-keywords/
Title: How to Rank for Local Keywords: A Practical Local SEO Guide
Description: How to rank for local keywords: local keyword research, website optimisation, Google Business Profile, citations, local links, schema and social.

When people search for something nearby, like "plumber near me" or "dentist in Boise", Google shows a short list of local businesses. Here's how to get yours into that list.

## 1. Find the right local keywords

Combine your services with your locations: "plumber in Boise" or "dentist Idaho Falls". Google Keyword Planner and Moz Keyword Explorer show volumes, and Google's autocomplete shows how people phrase them.

## 2. Optimise your website for local search

- Show your business name, address and phone number (NAP) consistently

- Create a page for each location or service area you serve

- Use local keywords in titles, headings and copy

- Embed a map and make the site fast and mobile-friendly

## 3. Optimise your Google Business Profile

Your Google Business Profile (formerly Google My Business) is what appears in the map pack. Choose accurate categories, add services, photos and opening hours, post updates and reply to every review.

## 4. Build local citations

Citations are mentions of your name, address and phone number on other sites. List your business on relevant directories, industry sites and your local chamber of commerce, with identical details everywhere.

## 5. Earn local backlinks

- Sponsor or take part in local events

- Write for local blogs and news sites

- Offer expert comment to local journalists

- Partner with complementary local businesses

## 6. Add local schema markup

LocalBusiness schema tells search engines your business type, address, hours and contact details. Add review markup only where it follows Google's guidelines.

## 7. Track rankings across your area

Local rankings change street by street. A grid-based tracker such as Local Falcon shows where you rank across your whole service area, not just from one spot.

There's no trick to local SEO. It's accurate details everywhere, a steady trickle of reviews and pages that genuinely help local customers, kept up month after month. Get in touch.

URL: https://anilsharma.co/google-analytics-4/
Title: Google Analytics 4: What You Need to Know | Anil Sharma
Description: A plain-English guide to Google Analytics 4: user-centric measurement, events, cross-platform tracking, predictive metrics and privacy controls.

Google Analytics 4 replaced the old Universal Analytics, and it measures things differently. You don't need to know all of it. These are the parts that matter most if you run a business.

## User-centric measurement

GA4 is built around users and events rather than sessions and pageviews. That makes it easier to see how the same person engages with you over time and across devices.

## Everything is an event

Clicks, scrolls, video plays, form submissions and purchases are all events. Many are tracked automatically with enhanced measurement, and the rest can be added through Google Tag Manager. Mark the important ones as key events (conversions).

## Cross-platform tracking

One GA4 property can collect data from your website and apps, giving a single view of the customer journey.

## Machine learning and predictive metrics

With enough data, GA4 predicts purchase probability and churn, and surfaces unusual changes automatically. These predictive audiences can be shared with Google Ads.

## Privacy and consent

GA4 offers more control over data collection and retention, and works with Consent Mode, which is now essential for advertisers in the EU and UK.

## Connect it to Google Ads and Search Console

Linking GA4 with Google Ads and Search Console brings search queries, ad costs and conversions into one place, and lets Google Ads bid using your GA4 key events.

GA4 is only as good as its setup. If your conversion numbers look odd, fix the tracking before you make any decisions based on them. Get in touch.

URL: https://anilsharma.co/local-seo-guide-for-small-businesses/
Title: Local SEO: A Step-by-Step Guide for Small Businesses
Description: A step-by-step local SEO guide for small businesses: website optimisation, Google Business Profile setup, citations, reviews and local backlinks.

Local SEO is what helps your business show up when people nearby look for what you sell. For many small businesses, it's the best-value marketing there is. Here's how to do it, step by step.

## Step 1: Optimise your website for local search

- Put your name, address and phone number on every page, usually in the footer

- Create a dedicated page for each location

- Use location keywords in titles, meta descriptions, headings and image alt text

- Add LocalBusiness schema markup

- Make sure the site is fast and mobile-friendly

## Step 2: Claim and optimise your Google Business Profile

Your Google Business Profile controls how you appear on Google Search and Maps.

- Claim and verify the profile

- Choose the most accurate primary category

- Add services, products, hours, photos and a description

- Post updates regularly

- Ask happy customers for reviews, and reply to all of them

## Step 3: Build local citations

List your business on reputable directories (industry sites, local directories, Yelp, Bing Places and Apple Business Connect) with exactly the same details everywhere.

## Step 4: Get links from local websites

- Partner with complementary local businesses

- Sponsor local events and get listed on their sites

- Create local guides and resources others want to link to

## Step 5: Measure and keep going

Track calls, direction requests and website clicks from your Business Profile, and watch local rankings across your area. Local SEO compounds when you keep adding reviews, photos and content.

If you'd rather hand it over, I look after Google Business Profiles and local SEO for businesses in the US, UK, Australia and here in India. Get in touch.
